content:
Hi Julien

There's two possible reasons why scanning the QR codes don't work.

1. Your desktops account's configuration is not supported by the mobile app. See bottom of page at: https://support.mozilla.org/km/kb/thunderbird-android-import

2. There have been a number of bug reports where devices are unable to scan QR Codes. This is being tracked at: https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/issues/8520

Have you compared the settings with those working on your desktop. Are they the same.

  • Imap v pop3.
  • User name & password v oAuth authentication.
  • Check password for typing errors.

As your email is a business or personal domain, it's not possible for others to check the imap settings in your screen shot are correct, compare with public services such as gmail.

content:
There's two additional ways you can add your accounts to the Redminote 12.

1. Use Thunderbird Android's wizard to manually add an account. Enter your email address. You'll be guided on additional steps to follow.

2. Export your account configuration from your Xiaomi and import it into your Redminote 12.

a. In TB on your Xiaomi tablet, goto settings > export. Save the configuration to a file. b. Copy the configuration file to your Redminote 12 c. In TB on the Redminote 12, goto settings > import. Select the configuration file.

The option to import a configuration or add a new account are available from the first time setup page,

QR code scanning Issues with QR code scanning have been reported and being tracked on the github ticket below. https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/issues/8520
